newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, trying to consolidate.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, trying to consolidate.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds mainly were flat in quiet, early trade Tuesday, trying to consolidate around higher levels hit over the past few days on views that economic growth was not strong enough to set off inflation.

"Bids pretty much opened where they closed yesterday. It's kind of a wait-and-see," a trader said, explaining that fixed income markets likely would have to wait for direction until the latest jobless claims were released on Thursday, followed by Producer Prices on Friday.

Another trader said: "It's sort of regrouping after a couple of up days Thursday and yesterday. There are a few customer bid-wanteds and a few Street bid-wanteds." Later, he added there was little follow-through after the recent rise.
And the softer tone displayed by the Treasury market easily could spill over into municipal bond prices if it persists.

The drop in yields evidently has started pulling new issues from the day-to-day calender, as the City and County of Denver and State of Colorado, School District Number 1, decided to sell Tuesday over $383 million of taxable, pension Certificates of Participation.
The deal follows New Jersey's recent sale of $2.75 billion of taxable, pension obligation bonds, which traders said have outperformed other instruments since they were issued.
"But the float is extremely thin," a trader added.
Municipal bond sales for Tuesday had been expected to total $431 million in 30 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Negotiated offerings added up to $273 million in six sales, with a $150 million Sacramento Municipal Utility District, Calif., deal through Goldman, Sachs & Co., topping the list.
On the competitive side, 24 sales totaling $158 million were scheduled. A $27 million Freehold Township Board of Education, N.J., deal at 1100 EDT was the largest.
In the secondary market, Lorain County, Ohio, Hospital Revenues Refunding-Catholic Healthcare Partners of 2027, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were offered at 99-1/2, down an eighth of a point.
Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey bonds of 2026, which pay a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 99-7/8, flat.
September Treasury bond futures shed three ticks to 113-18/32, while September municipal bond futures eased two ticks to 118-30/32. This left the MOB spread one tick up at plus 172 ticks.
